interactions.Spatial & Ocean Explanation: Typical (+0.31): the rate is only moderately elevated (rate anomaly +0.56; 75th percentile). The centroid moved 133 km with 0% outside the historical 90% area. High chlorophyll-a and distance-to-seamount percentiles (both 94.7th), plus cooler SST (10.5th), indicate unusual habitat use, but not enough to produce an unusual interaction count.

Upper-typical (+0.93): the elevated count agrees with a high rate anomaly (+0.95; 95th percentile). A 283 km centroid shift remains entirely inside the historical 90% area. High chlorophyll-a (89.5th) and distance-to-seamount (94.7th), with cooler SST (21.1st), provide environmental context for the increase.

Low but typical (-1.10): the depressed count is consistent with a low rate anomaly (-0.99), a 20th-percentile rate, and a 30.7% annual decline. The 766 km centroid shift is the largest of all species, although 0% falls outside the broad historical 90% area. Very high sea-level anomaly (94.4th) and low SST percentile (11.1st) mark a substantially different interaction environment.

Typical (+0.58): interactions are above the historical median, but the rate anomaly is modest (+0.33; 55th percentile) and the recent rate trend is decreasing (-16.5% annually). The centroid shifted 311 km and 5.9% of interactions are outside the historical 90% area. High chlorophyll-a (90th) and distance-to-seamount (95th), with cooler SST (15th), suggest redistribution rather than a strong abundance anomaly.

Upper-typical (+1.01): the elevated count aligns with a positive rate anomaly (+0.65), a 65th-percentile rate, and a 7.1% annual increase. The centroid moved 178 km and 12.5% of interactions lie outside the historical 90% area—the largest outside share. Ocean signals are mixed to moderate, so spatial expansion and rising rate provide the stronger explanation.

High (+3.24): the exceptional count is supported by a strong rate anomaly (+1.70), an 85th-percentile rate, and 5.1% annual growth. The centroid shift is only 61 km—the smallest—so the spike is not mainly a large relocation effect; 5.4% lies outside the historical 90% area. High chlorophyll-a (88.9th), greater distance to seamounts (83.3rd), and cooler SST (22.2nd) characterize the conditions accompanying the high interactions.
